title: Curriculum ({{ stores.curriculum.name }} SSOT store)
description: Schema for the {{ stores.curriculum.name }} SSOT store ({{ stores.curriculum.path }}), written by curriculum-sequencer. Sequences the {{ stores.design.name }} graph's taught nodes (Baseline excluded) into sessions of ordered lessons, embedded checkpoints, and assessments, each carrying a delivery style so downstream tools can pick a material-generation strategy per item. Node ids referenced by `node_ref` must exist in {{ stores.design.path }}.

sessions.description: Ordered delivery sessions. Order in this array is the delivery order.

persona_ref.description: A persona id from {{ stores.student_personas.name }}/{{ stores.design.name }} for this course (e.g. P-DEV, P-DBA, P-PM — any persona set the course defines), or "shared" when a task is not lane-specific.

didactic_activity.description: The pedagogical shape of the item. Drives which material-generation strategy a downstream tool applies (e.g. lecture -> slide deck, hands_on_practical -> exercise sheet + starter repo, briefing -> handout only). "lecture": one-way conceptual presentation, no live demo, no built-in discussion stop. "lecture_discussion": lecture with deliberate stops for questions/opinions/comparing the group's own experience; still no one touches a system. "lecture_demo": instructor presents and also drives a live system in front of the group (they watch, don't type) — use when the concept must be seen running, not just described. "group_discussion": students talk to each other with no instructor exposition first; the discussion itself is the point. "hands_on_practical": students execute a scoped exercise themselves, tied to one specific node/skill, normally with one clear expected outcome. "project_based": open-ended activity integrating multiple already-taught nodes/skills, less scripted than hands_on_practical, may have more than one valid solution path. "briefing": short one-way informational announcement with no instructional depth (logistics, credentials) — not teaching a skill.

item.description: One row of the sequence table: a taught node, an embedded DR checkpoint, or an assessment.

sequence.description: Display order key as used in the source doc (e.g. "1", "A1", "13"). Array position is authoritative for ordering; this is for cross-referencing the human-readable doc.

node_ref.description: Id(s) of the {{ stores.design.name }} node(s) this item teaches or checks (e.g. PRQ-SCG-BASICS, DR-DEPLOY-GATEWAY). A single id for an item that teaches or checks one node. An array of ids for an item that spans several nodes at once (e.g. a prerequisite-check quiz covering every Baseline a unit assumes) — never invent a separate field name for this case. Omitted entirely for a pure cross-DR assessment scoped to "all nodes in the course", such as a summative final exam or the capstone, where enumerating every node adds no information. Required (in one of its two shapes) for item_type lesson and checkpoint.

didactic_activity.description: Required for item_type lesson; a checkpoint or assessment may omit it (see assessment_kind instead) or reuse the enclosing lesson's style.

duration_minutes.description: Minutes budgeted for this item. Null for a checkpoint embedded inside another item's time (see embedded_in).

notes.description: Free-text asides (e.g. why this item's rubric/timing looks the way it does).

target_minutes.description: The target teaching/assessment minutes for this session (may be below usable_minutes to leave buffer).

usable_minutes.description: Usable minutes in the session block after accounting for setup/breaks/friction, per {{ stores.logistics.name }}.

total_minutes.description: Sum of this session's items' duration_minutes (null durations contribute 0). Provided for cross-check against a tool's own recomputation.
